title: [Lean] Link an end-to-end proof of multiplication below n log n
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Add a pointer under “Research notes and verification contributions” to [Dan Brown](https://github.com/jdb19937) and [Kenny Daniel](https://github.com/platypii)'s end-to-end Lean proof of integer multiplication below n log n on Mathlib's finite Turing machines. The paragraph states the explicit exponent saving and the theorem's exact transitive axiom dependencies.

## Task and overlap

Documentation pointer to an external completed proof, based on upstream `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`. The linked result uses κ = 296 / (10^11 · 2^131); it does not establish the selected conditional exponent saving.

## Validation

Checked that the diff only adds the paragraph to README.md. The external proof's pinned source is [7415d77](https://github.com/platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean/tree/7415d773d14212c68b523979aaac6db9dc0ba542): [statement](https://github.com/platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean/blob/7415d773d14212c68b523979aaac6db9dc0ba542/IntegerMultBounds/MathlibTM2/Statement.lean), [theorem](https://github.com/platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean/blob/7415d773d14212c68b523979aaac6db9dc0ba542/IntegerMultBounds/MathlibTM2/Theorem.lean), and [completed-proof axiom audit](https://github.com/platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean/blob/7415d773d14212c68b523979aaac6db9dc0ba542/CompletedProofCheck.lean). Its [Linux CI run](https://github.com/platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean/actions/runs/38699796435) passed the build and all four axiom/check entry points on Lean and Mathlib v4.34.1. No new Lean build or historical certificate replay was run for this README-only change.

## Credit

[Dan Brown](https://github.com/jdb19937) and [Kenny Daniel](https://github.com/platypii) are credited as the proof's coauthors. The external proof remains in its MIT-licensed repository; this PR contributes only the README pointer.

## Open next questions

Independent review of the linked theorem statement and machine/time model.

Improve the formally proved runtime bound to match the current state of the art, starting with the selected conditional exponent saving κ = 0.001672660197076918, while retaining the end-to-end machine proof and the same standard axiom dependencies.
